title: Will Your Ex Come Back?

plan.title: How it ended, and what the clock says
Why you still check their profile
Too much of one thing, none of another
So, will they come back? The honest answer
What you do now (Yeon wrote a plan)

options.label: We both did, more or less
It faded out, or it's complicated

intake.question: How long ago did it end?
What do you want right now, honestly?

me.speaker: yeon
me.text: You said you ended it. And you're still here reading about them. Interesting.

them.speaker: bom
them.text: They ended it. So you didn't get a vote. That's a specific kind of hurt, and we'll be gentle with it.

mutual.speaker: yeon
mutual.text: "We both did, more or less." The "more or less" is doing a lot of work there.

unclear.speaker: bom
unclear.text: It faded out. No big fight, no clean ending. Those are the ones that stay open the longest.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You skipped who ended it. Which means the answer is complicated, or it still stings.

fresh.speaker: bom
fresh.text: Less than a month. Everything is still loud right now. Nothing you feel this week is a final answer.

months.speaker: yeon
months.text: One to six months. The "I'm totally fine" phase, followed by one song in a supermarket ruining your whole Thursday.

half.speaker: yeon
half.text: Six to twelve months, and they're still in your head rent-free. Time to look at the lease.

long.speaker: bom
long.text: Over a year. If it still pulls at you, it's not about missing them. It's about something they touched that's still open.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You didn't say how long. Which usually means "longer than I'd admit at brunch".

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart, so let's talk about your part. You don't lose arguments. You win them. Every single one.

Bom: Winning a fight and keeping a person are two different sports.

Yeon: You were so busy being right you didn't notice them getting quieter.

Think of one fight you "won". Now replay it from their side, in one sentence. That sentence is probably closer to why it ended than anything they said at the end.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You won every argument. Look where it got you. Single, and correct.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You gave and gave, and somewhere in there you stopped saying what you needed.

Yeon: Then one day you were resentful and they had no idea why. Because you never told them.

Bom: That's not a failure of love. It's a failure of volume.

Name one thing you needed and never said out loud. Just one. Keep it. It's the first line of your next relationship.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You loved quietly. Next time, love a little louder.

rat.text: The Rat sits closest to your heart: clever, private, awake at night. You probably saw the cracks early and kept the information to yourself. In the next one, share the intel.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat heart: you clocked every warning sign. Then filed it under "later".

ox.text: The Ox guards your heart: loyal, slow, steady. You stayed longer than made sense because leaving felt like breaking a promise. Loyalty is beautiful. So is knowing when it's done.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox heart: you don't leave easily. That's why this hurts so much.

tiger.text: The Tiger sits in your heart: brave, proud, independent. You'd rather suffer in private than look like you're begging. Wanting them back isn't weakness. Pretending you don't care is just armour.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger heart: you'd rather lose them than lose face. Noted.

rabbit.text: The Rabbit lives close to your heart: gentle, charming, conflict-shy. You kept things smooth until smooth stopped being honest. Next time, one small fight early saves one big ending later.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit heart: keeping the peace isn't the same as having it.

dragon.text: The Dragon guards your heart: big dreams, big expectations. You wanted something legendary, and anything less felt like settling. Some of that is standards. Some of it is a story nobody could live up to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon heart: you wanted an epic. They wanted a Tuesday.

snake.text: The Snake sits closest to your heart: intuitive, private, strategic. You read them perfectly and showed them very little. They loved someone they never fully saw.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Snake heart: you saw everything. They saw a closed door.

horse.text: The Horse lives in your heart: passionate, restless, freedom first. When it felt like a fence, you ran, even if you only ran in your head. The right person won't feel like a fence.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Horse heart: you need open fields. That was always allowed.

goat.text: The Goat guards your heart: gentle, homey, needs reassurance. You needed to hear "we're okay" more than they said it. Next time, ask for it. Plainly. It's not too much.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat heart: needing reassurance isn't needy. It's how you're built.

monkey.text: The Monkey sits in your heart: clever, playful, bores easily. The banter was the best part, and when the banter faded you wondered what was left. Fun matters. So does what's under it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey heart: you miss the jokes more than the person. Be honest.

rooster.text: The Rooster guards your heart: proud, precise, critical. You saw what was wrong and said so, often. You were usually right. Being right was lonely by the end.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rooster heart: you had notes. On everything. They got tired of notes.

dog.text: The Dog lives close to your heart: loyal, protective, principled. You stayed loyal past the point it was good for you. That loyalty is a gift. Give it to someone who guards it back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dog heart: so loyal. Next time, to someone who's loyal back.

pig.text: The Pig sits in your heart: sweet, generous, trusting. You gave second chances like party favours. Kindness isn't the mistake. Ignoring your own red flags is.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pig heart: you forgave things you should've at least mentioned.

day_branch_heading: Who you let in close: the {day_animal} ({day_branch})

base.why-it-ended:
Trees grow straight up. That's your gift. It's also why, when they wanted to go sideways, you just kept growing.

Yeon: You heard "I need space" and replied with a plan for more structure.

Bom: You were trying to save it.

Yeon: You were trying to manage it. They wanted to be asked, not led.

Bom: You're not the villain here. You're the one who never let go of the wheel, even when they were asking to drive for a bit.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You loved hard and planned a whole future. You had the next five years in a notes app.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And you never asked if they wanted to be in the notes app.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You don't bend. When it got hard, you fixed and explained. That's how you love. It just isn't how everyone hears it.

spring.intro: Spring birthday. That's tree season, so you got a double shot of yourself: taller, louder, surer. In saju terms, Wood ran the month you were born in. In real life, you've never once waited to be picked.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Double Wood. So the stubbornness is seasonal AND personal. Great.

summer.intro: You're a tree born in the heat. All that growing goes straight into showing: big plans, big talk, big gestures. Summer burns through a pine fast, so you look unstoppable right up until you suddenly need three days in bed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give off so much light. Just save a little for yourself.

autumn.intro: Autumn is axe season, and you're the tree. Life started trimming you early: rules, pressure, people with opinions. It made you sharper and more disciplined than other pines. It also made you allergic to being told what to do.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pruned young. Explains the posture. And the attitude.

winter.intro: A winter pine. The cold kept you quiet on the outside while the roots drank everything. You think longer than you let on, and when you finally move, it's because you already decided weeks ago.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You look calm. Underneath, you've been planning since November.

earth.intro: Born in the between-season weeks, when soil runs the show. For a tree, that means work: you're always building, fixing, providing. Very useful. Very tired. Somebody should ask what you want for once.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rest is not a prize you win. It's allowed.

open.title: You had a five-year plan. They had a different one.
open.text:
You're not someone who looks back. You plan forward. And yet here you are, at night, scrolling to a photo from two summers ago.

Bom: You miss them.

Yeon: You miss being right about where it was going.
open.end: Bom: Before we answer "will they come back", we need the part nobody told you about why it ended. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Pine, in one line: you don't leave, you | outgrow. And then you blame them for staying small.

sample.text: If they reach out, don't answer with a plan. Answer with a question.

base.why-it-ended:
Vines climb what's there. You found them and grew all over their life. Lovely, until they needed you to be your own wall for a minute.

Yeon: You said "I don't mind" so many times they stopped asking what you minded.

Bom: You avoided fights to keep it safe.

Yeon: And the unsaid stuff built up until it was the only thing in the room.

Bom: It didn't end because you were too much. If anything, you let yourself be too little.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You made yourself fit their life so easily. You were so good at loving them.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: So good you disappeared. They broke up with a version of you that agreed with everything.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You wrapped your whole life around them. When they left, you lost the shape of your days, not just them.

spring.intro: Spring birthday for the vine. Everything around you was growing, so you learned to grow toward whatever held still long enough. Charming. Flexible. Absolutely capable of getting your way while people believe they chose it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Double Wood vine. You don't push. You wrap. Same result.

summer.intro: A flower in full sun. You bloom in public: the outfit, the story, the laugh across the room. The cost is that you wilt on the inside when nobody's watering you, and you'd rather die than ask.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're so easy to love. You just don't always let anyone try.

autumn.intro: Autumn is cutting season, and you're the soft stem. You grew up reading rooms for danger, learning who's sharp and how to bend before they swing. That's why you're so good with people. It's also why you apologise to furniture.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You flinch at "can we talk" like it's a fire alarm.

winter.intro: A winter flower. Cold outside, so you grew inward: rich head, private feelings, a whole inner world nobody gets the password to. When you trust someone, it's total. Getting there takes a season.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your inside is so much warmer than you let people see.

earth.intro: Born in the weeks between seasons, when the soil takes over. For a vine, that means you grow by managing things: schedules, people, plans. You're the reason the group trip happened. Nobody thanked you properly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Unpaid project manager of every friendship. Since birth.

open.title: You didn't just lose them. You lost the version of you that fit them.
open.text:
Their favourite show became your favourite show. Their friends became your weekends. Now you're standing in the middle of your own life going "wait, what do I like?"

Bom: You adapt because you love.

Yeon: You adapt so well that nobody, including you, can find you afterwards.
open.end: Yeon: And the reason it ended has a lot to do with that disappearing act. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Flower: you never leave first. You just | get quieter and quieter until they do it for you.

sample.text: If they text, reply like someone with plans. Because you'll have some by then.

base.why-it-ended:
You give warmth on full blast. But warmth on full blast can feel like a spotlight, and some people get tired of being lit up.

Yeon: Or you got tired of shining at someone who stopped shining back.

Bom: You need to feel seen. When they stopped noticing, it hurt more than a fight would.

Yeon: And instead of saying "I feel invisible", you got louder. Bigger. More.

Bom: It ended somewhere between you giving more and them noticing less.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You gave them so much warmth. You made them feel like the main character.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And then you posted a gym selfie the day after the breakup. Very healed. Very normal.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You shine brightest when you're hurting most. People think you're fine. You're not, and that's okay.

spring.intro: The sun, born in spring. Everything was feeding you: new leaves, longer days, people who wanted your attention. So you grew up assuming warmth is normal. When someone's cold to you, it genuinely confuses you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooms get brighter when you arrive. That is not nothing.

summer.intro: The sun at noon in July. Double fire. You don't enter rooms, you arrive. Generous, loud, impossible to ignore, and secretly a little hurt every time someone doesn't notice you lit the place up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Main character, sequel, director's cut. All you.

autumn.intro: An autumn sun. Lower in the sky, aimed at things: harvest, goals, results. You're warm, but you're also counting. You notice exactly who showed up for you and who just liked the post.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Warm and keeping score. Your sunshine comes with receipts.

winter.intro: A winter sun. Short days, cold air, people who needed you more than they could give back. It made you tough and a little performative: the brightest one in the room, even on the days you're running on fumes.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You shine hardest when you're the most tired. I see it.

earth.intro: Born in the between-season weeks, when Earth runs things. For the sun, that means everything you give turns into something solid: a friend's confidence, a plan that worked, a party you made happen. You're a great investment. Ask what you're getting back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You fund everyone's glow-up and forget to invoice.

open.title: You posted "thriving" the next day. You were not thriving.
open.text:
You're the sun. Breakups don't dim you in public. You go out, you're the life of the dinner, you post the story. Then you go home and check if they watched it.

Bom: You hide hurt behind light.

Yeon: You turned a breakup into a comeback tour with one fan you're trying to impress.
open.end: Bom: Here's what the brightness was covering, even before it ended. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Sun: you don't end things. You | burn so bright they either keep up or burn out. Most burn out.

sample.text: If they reach out, do not perform "I'm thriving" at them. Just be thriving. Elsewhere.

base.why-it-ended:
You give quiet, intense attention. You notice everything. And when something hurt you, you didn't say it. You filed it.

Yeon: You kept a private archive of every small letdown. They didn't know there was an archive.

Bom: You were waiting for them to notice on their own.

Yeon: Babe, they were not psychic. You were hinting at someone who reads instructions.

Bom: It ended in the gap between what you felt and what you said.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You loved them in the quiet, close way. The way nobody else noticed.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You still know their schedule. And their mum's birthday. And their Spotify. You need a hobby.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You hold the small moments. The coffee order. The look. That's why letting go takes you longer.

spring.intro: A candle lit in spring. Fed from every side, so your warmth is steady and close: one person, one conversation, the whole night. You'd take a deep two-hour talk over a party of fifty every single time.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: When you pay attention to someone, they feel chosen.

summer.intro: A candle in midsummer. Double fire, so the flame runs hot: intense focus, intense loyalty, intense feelings you insist are "fine". You don't do half anything. That includes holding a grudge.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You remember a tone of voice from 2019. Word for word.

autumn.intro: A candle in autumn, burning toward a goal. You're quietly ambitious, a little perfectionist, and you light up most when you're useful. The danger is that you start to believe useful is the only way to be loved.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to earn the warmth you give everyone else.

winter.intro: A candle in winter. Cold all around, so your small flame matters more. You grew up being the warm one in a chilly place, which made you protective, careful, and very good at sensing a mood change from the next room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can hear a sigh through a closed door. Through two.

earth.intro: Born in the soil weeks between seasons. Your candle burns into the ground: caring, fixing, holding people together. You make every space feel like home. You also over-give until the wax runs out.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You hosted everyone's crisis. Who's hosting yours?

open.title: You still know which song they'd skip.
open.text:
You loved one person like a candle loves a dark room: completely, quietly, for hours. Now the room's empty and you're still burning.

Bom: Your devotion is real.

Yeon: Your devotion currently has no recipient and very high running costs.
open.end: Yeon: And the thing that ended it wasn't the thing you keep replaying. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Candle: you stay long after it's over, because | leaving would mean the flame was for nothing. It wasn't.

sample.text: If they reach out, don't reply at midnight. Nothing good was ever typed by a candle at midnight.

base.why-it-ended:
You're solid. Reliable. The same on Monday as on Friday. For a while that felt like safety to them.

Yeon: Then it started to feel like talking to a very supportive wall.

Bom: You do feel things. Deeply. You just don't announce them.

Yeon: They asked "what are you thinking?" a hundred times and got "nothing" ninety-nine of them.

Bom: It didn't end because you didn't care. It ended because they couldn't see that you did.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You were their safe place. Steady, calm, always there.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Always there, never moving. Mountains are great for hiking. Terrible at "can we talk about us".

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You don't show the cracks. You just hold. Even now, you're holding it together in public.

spring.intro: A mountain in spring, with trees pushing through it from every side. Life tested you early. That's why you're so steady now, and also why "relax" sounds to you like a trick.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You became the calm one because someone had to.

summer.intro: A summer mountain, warmed all the way through. Solid, generous, the one everyone leans on. You give off safety without trying. People tell you things they've never told anyone, and you never repeat them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: People feel safe with you within five minutes. Rare.

autumn.intro: An autumn mountain, showing its stone. You turn your weight into output: work done, things built, problems quietly solved. You don't talk about feelings much. You show them by fixing the shelf.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Love language: unasked-for repairs. Every time.

winter.intro: A mountain in winter, holding back the river. You manage things: money, plans, other people's chaos. Very good at it. The cost is that you rarely let anything thaw, including you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're not cold. You're frozen on purpose. Different.

earth.intro: A mountain born in Earth's own weeks. Triple solid. You don't move unless you want to, and you almost never want to. Your loyalty is legendary. So is the time it takes you to change your mind.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Persuading you is a geological process.

open.title: You're "fine". Mountains are always "fine".
open.text:
You didn't cry in front of anyone. You went to work. You answered emails. You were completely fine, except for the part where you weren't.

Bom: You carry it so nobody else has to.

Yeon: You carry it so nobody notices. Then you wonder why nobody noticed.
open.end: Bom: The steadiness everyone loves about you? It played a part in how this ended. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Mountain: you don't fight for it. You | wait for it to fix itself, and it never once has.

sample.text: If they reach out, say one honest sentence. Not "all good". An actual sentence with a feeling in it.

base.why-it-ended:
You give, you smooth things over, you make it work. And you assumed that if you kept giving, it would keep working.

Bom: You wanted them to feel looked after.

Yeon: You wanted them to need you so much they'd never leave. Close cousin. Different animal.

Bom: Somewhere in there, you started managing the relationship instead of being in it.

Yeon: They had a partner and a project manager in one person. Nobody likes their project manager.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You looked after them so well. Their bad days, their deadlines, their family stuff.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And now you're worried about how THEY'RE coping. They dumped you. Read that back.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You look after everyone. Even the person who hurt you. That's how kind you are.

spring.intro: A garden in spring, with everything sprouting from you at once. You grew up being needed: the friend who listens, the kid who helped. Lovely trait. Exhausting default.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You nourish everybody. Your turn next.

summer.intro: Garden soil in summer, warm and rich. You're nurturing on instinct and practical about it: snacks in the bag, charger for everyone, a plan B nobody asked for. Everyone feels a bit safer near you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You packed plasters for a picnic. Twice.

autumn.intro: A harvest-season garden. Everything you grow, you hand out. Ideas, help, advice, food. The harvest is real, but so is the empty field afterwards, and you never schedule time to grow back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Giving is your gift. Refilling is your homework.

winter.intro: A winter garden. Frozen on top, busy underneath. You worry productively: lists, backups, a mental spreadsheet of who needs what. You keep it together for everyone, and you'd never admit you're scared too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You overthink in organised folders. Colour-coded.

earth.intro: Soil born in soil weeks. Double Earth. You're the steady one, the reliable one, the one who remembers birthdays. You can also absorb other people's moods like a sponge and call it "being supportive".

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Their mood, your weekend. Every time.

open.title: They left, and you're worried they're not eating properly.
open.text:
You were the one who remembered the appointments, kept snacks in the car, checked in when their week was bad. You built them a softer life. Now the softness has nowhere to go.

Bom: You're a natural carer.

Yeon: You're an unpaid carer with no client. Take the week off.
open.end: Yeon: And yes, the caring is part of the story of why it ended. Not the way you think. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Field: you pick people you can | help, and then you're hurt when they leave once they're better.

sample.text: If they reach out, check whether they want you or want your help. Both feel the same at first.

base.why-it-ended:
You're a blade: clear, direct, built to protect. You fixed problems fast. You told the truth even when nobody asked.

Yeon: "I'm just being honest" is your favourite sentence. They heard it a lot.

Bom: You were honest because you cared. Truly.

Yeon: Sure. But honesty with no softness feels like a review, not a relationship.

Bom: It ended somewhere between you being right and them wanting to feel safe.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You were so loyal. You'd have gone to war for them. Honestly, you did, a few times.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Also told them exactly what they were doing wrong. Weekly. Unprompted. With examples.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You protect people by being honest. It's love. It just doesn't always sound like love.

spring.intro: A blade born in spring, surrounded by things to cut. You see what needs doing and you do it, preferably before anyone has finished explaining. Efficient. Also sometimes the reason the meeting went badly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You solved their problem. They wanted a hug. Classic.

summer.intro: A sword forged in summer. Heat everywhere, so you were shaped by pressure: deadlines, expectations, people who pushed. It made you strong and principled. It also made you assume love is a test you can fail.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to pass anything. You're already loved.

autumn.intro: A sword born in autumn, metal's own season. Double steel. Loyal to the bone, blunt as a brick, and fair in a way that scares people. You'd fight anyone for a friend, and tell that friend exactly where they went wrong on the way home.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd take a bullet for a friend. Then critique their aim.

winter.intro: A blade in winter. Cold, clear, and sharpened by thinking. You say less than other Swords, but when you speak it lands like a verdict. People quote you back to yourself years later.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your words stay with people. Choose the kind ones too.

earth.intro: A sword still in the stone. Born in the soil weeks, so you were held, fed and protected before you were ever swung. That gives you patience most Swords lack, and a stubborn streak made of actual rock.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Patient, until you're not. Then it's a sword.

open.title: You'd have died for them. You just wouldn't say sorry.
open.text:
You'll fix their car, defend them in public, and never once say "I miss you" out loud. Breakups don't make you cry. They make you go to the gym and lift something very heavy.

Bom: You process by doing.

Yeon: You process by not processing. With weights.
open.end: Bom: There's one thing you never said in the whole relationship. It's on the next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Sword: you'd rather end it clean than | admit you're scared. So you cut first, every time.

sample.text: If they reach out, skip the verdict. They didn't text for a performance review.

base.why-it-ended:
You're a jewel. High standards, sharp eye, and you notice every little thing that's off. In love, that eye didn't switch off.

Yeon: You noticed every flaw. They noticed you noticing.

Bom: You also needed so much reassurance and asked for so little.

Yeon: So you tested them instead. Little silences. Little cold moments. To see if they'd chase.

Bom: It ended somewhere between your standards and your fear of not meeting theirs.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You gave them the polished, beautiful version of you. That took effort.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: In the shower version, you win. Every time. Shame it's not on record.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You feel things sharply. One careless sentence from them can still cut, months later.

spring.intro: A jewel born in spring. Everything was growing and you noticed all of it: what's pretty, what's off, what's three millimetres crooked. You have taste. You also have opinions about other people's taste.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You judged the font on their birthday card. Silently.

summer.intro: A jewel in summer heat. Pressure shaped you: to look good, do well, never be the embarrassing one. You're polished and impressive. One careless comment can still ruin your whole week.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to be unfinished. It's charming, honestly.

autumn.intro: A jewel born in metal's own season. Double shine. High standards, sharp eye, zero patience for sloppy. You're the friend people dress up for. You're also the friend people are slightly scared to disappoint.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're a five-star review. With a long comment section.

winter.intro: A jewel in winter water, washed clear. Your mind is quick and your words are precise. You can say one sentence that fixes everything, or one that ends everything. Most of the time you know which.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You see people so clearly. Use it to be kind.

earth.intro: A jewel still in the earth. Born in the soil weeks, so you were protected, maybe a little over-protected. You need to feel safe before you sparkle, and that's not a flaw. It's quality control.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You need three green flags before one selfie.

open.title: You've replayed the last conversation forty times. With edits.
open.text:
You know exactly what you should have said. You've written it in your head, polished it, delivered it to an imaginary them in the shower. Perfect every time.

Bom: You want to get it right.

Yeon: You want to win a conversation that ended in March.
open.end: Yeon: The real reason it ended isn't in that conversation, by the way. It's on the next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Jewel: you leave a tiny bit early, so | nobody ever gets the chance to leave you first.

sample.text: If they reach out, don't draft for an hour. The perfect reply is the one that sounds like you.

base.why-it-ended:
You need freedom like other people need sleep. When things got close, part of you started looking for the exit.

Yeon: You didn't leave. You just drifted. Further out every week.

Bom: You weren't trying to hurt them. You were trying to breathe.

Yeon: And they felt you drifting and had no idea how to pull you back in.

Bom: It ended in the space between your need for room and their need for you to stay in it.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You loved them in a big, deep, oceanic way. That kind of love doesn't just switch off.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You've done a full documentary on the breakup. Narrated. Starring them as the problem.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You need space to breathe. That was never wrong. It just needed explaining.

spring.intro: The ocean in spring, pouring itself into everything that grows. You're full of ideas and you give them away: plans, pep talks, 3am theories. People feel bigger around you. You sometimes feel emptier after.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You make people feel possible. Keep a little for you.

summer.intro: The ocean in summer, chasing everything. Big appetite for life: trips, people, projects, the next thing. You're magnetic and hard to pin down. Being pinned down is honestly your nightmare.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You said "let's see where it goes". You meant "don't make me commit".

autumn.intro: The ocean in autumn, fed by every stream. Deep, informed, a little too clever. You absorb everything and you can talk your way out of anything. That includes your own feelings.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You intellectualise heartbreak. With footnotes.

winter.intro: The ocean in winter. Double water. Deep, cold on top, enormous underneath. You need a lot of freedom and you think in huge loops. People call you mysterious. You just haven't decided yet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your depth scares shallow people. That's their problem.

earth.intro: An ocean held by cliffs. Born in the soil weeks, so you grew up with banks and rules around you. It gave you focus. It also left you with a quiet itch to flood something just to prove you can.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You follow every rule. Until one random Tuesday.

open.title: You have eleven theories about why it ended. None of them are about you.
open.text:
By day you're philosophical about it. "It wasn't meant to be." By night you're deep in a spiral of what-ifs, alternate endings and their Spotify.

Bom: You think in big waves.

Yeon: You think in very big circles that end exactly where they started.
open.end: Bom: There's one wave you keep swimming away from. Let's look at it. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Ocean: when it gets real, you get | busy. New plans, new people, new reasons you were never really in it.

sample.text: If they reach out, decide what you want before you reply. Not after three days of vibes.

base.why-it-ended:
You're rain: soft, quiet, everywhere. You sensed every mood and adjusted around it before they even knew they had one.

Yeon: You read their mind and kept yours locked.

Bom: You stayed quiet to keep the peace.

Yeon: The peace was fake. You were having a whole relationship in your head, alone.

Bom: It ended in everything you felt and never said.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You felt everything in that relationship. Every shift, every mood. You knew before they did.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You knew it was ending months before it ended. And you said nothing. Bold strategy.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your intuition is so strong. It saw this coming. That's why it hurts in such a quiet way.

spring.intro: Spring rain. You feed everything around you without anyone noticing it was you. You sense moods, fix vibes, water other people's plants. Quietly essential. Quietly forgotten. Not anymore.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Everything grows a little when you're around.

summer.intro: Rain in summer, gone the moment it lands. You chase what you want in quiet, clever ways, and you vanish when a room gets too loud. People find you fascinating. They also never quite know where you went.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You left the party without saying bye. Again. Iconic.

autumn.intro: Autumn rain, fed by cool clean air. Intuitive to the point of spooky. You know who's lying, who's sad, and who's about to text before your phone even lights up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your gut is right more often than your decisions are.

winter.intro: Winter rain. Double water. Still, deep, mostly internal. You feel everything at full volume and show about four percent of it. Your notes app has more emotional range than most novels.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your quiet isn't empty. It's full.

earth.intro: Rain falling on hard ground. Born in the soil weeks, so you met walls early: rules, expectations, people who didn't get you. You learned to soak in slowly instead of crashing through. Patient. Persistent. Underrated.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't fight walls. You just wear them down. Over years.

open.title: You knew it was over before they did. You said nothing.
open.text:
You felt the temperature change. The shorter replies. The way they said your name differently. You noticed in September. It ended in December. You spent three months pretending you hadn't noticed.

Bom: You were hoping you were wrong.

Yeon: You're never wrong about people. That's the annoying part.
open.end: Yeon: So why didn't you say anything? That's the real question. Next page.

cliff.text: Yeon: Your breakup pattern, Rain: you see the end coming and | quietly let it happen, so at least you were right.

sample.text: If they reach out, trust the first feeling in your stomach. Not the fifth. The first.
